in_arabic.name: شبيه
in_arabic.meaning: مشابه شبيه في الخَلق أو الصفات
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مشتق من الفعل شبه يَشبه شَبها وشُبها إذا تشابه وتساوى في الخَلق أو الصفات، ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران الآية 59 حيث قال تعالى {إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَى عِندَ اللَّهِ كَآدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ}، ويدل على الشخص الذي يحمل صفات مشابهة لشخص آخر، وقد استخدم في التراث الإسلامي للدلالة على النبي عيسى عليه السلام كونه شبيهًا بالإنسان العادي في الخَلق ولكن مع خصائص إلهية

in_urdu.name: شبیہ

in_english.name: Shabih
in_english.long_meaning: The name Shabih originates from the Arabic root 'sh-b-h', meaning 'to resemble' or 'to be similar'. In Islamic tradition, Shabih is used to describe someone or something that bears a likeness or resemblance to another. The Quranic reference to Shabih can be found in Surah Al Imran, Verse 59, where it discusses the likeness of Jesus to Adam. The name Shabih signifies a person with similar characteristics or attributes to another, often implying a spiritual or moral resemblance. Historically, the term has been used in Islamic theology to discuss the nature of prophetic and divine beings. Today, Shabih is used across various Muslim cultures as a given name, symbolizing the aspiration to emulate noble qualities

data.cultural_impact: The name "Shabih" holds immense cultural significance in Arabic-speaking communities, as it is derived from the root word "shabaha" which means 'to resemble' or 'to be like.' In contemporary context, "Shabih" can be perceived as an Arabic name that signifies the idea of being 'bestowed,' 'given' or 'received as a gift.' For instance, a child may be named Shabih, suggesting they were bestowed upon their parents with love and blessings. Additionally, in Islamic literature and history, numerous examples exist where Prophets, Saints, and scholars bestowed great blessings upon their followers by passing on their knowledge and wisdom. The name "Shabih" thus pays homage to such spiritual lineages and serves as a reminder of the divine gifting that often shapes our lives and destinies.
data.spiritual_significance: Moreover, in a spiritual context, the name "Shabih" takes on deeper resonance, as it hints at the concept of Divine favor and grace. In Islam, the belief that Allah (God) is the bestower of all blessings is a fundamental tenet. The Quran verse 32:5 states: "Many were the walis (guardians, protectors) before you whom we granted favors, and amongst them were those whom we preferred above others. Among them was 'Ali, son of Abi Talib." This verse refers to 'Ali as one who was bestowed with Divine favor and was granted the position of a guardian and protector (wali) for the Muslim community.
